It started at noon with a door I'd never walked through. It ended somewhere familiar that I suddenly saw clearly. Two filters, two species, one very good Friday — and the short walk in between that made all the difference.

32 Cup 01 · Noon · a first visit

A new door, on the second floor.Equate · Colombia, Huila — La Pradera

I'd never been to Equate. Found it up a flight of stairs — pastel, pared-back, genuinely spacious, a couple of dogs wandering the floor. Ordered the pour-over: a washed Gesha, exactly my kind of thing. The room won me over before the cup even arrived.

"Hot for the first two pours to build the aromatics — then we drop right down to 68–70°C for the last two, to finish clean and keep the bitterness out."
— the barista, on the descending pour
Pours 1–2  ·  90–92°C  — aromatics & malic acid
Pours 3–4  ·  68–70°C  — restraint, clean finish

The roaster promised

Peach jam · orange · honey sweetness.

The cup delivered

Peach arrived loud and clear — but a little alone. The honeyed, jammy sweetness behind it stayed shy, and the malic acidity ran a step ahead of everything meant to round it out. Clean and tea-like; I kept wanting it to fill in.

A 1:14 ratio front-loads the bright, fast-extracting acids — so the peach sings, while the slower sugars never quite catch up. A touch more water, and the orange and honey would have had room to bloom.

33 Cup 02 · 15:15 · a return, seen anew

The room I thought I knew.Corner Corner · Malaysia — My Liberica

I'd been to Corner Corner once before. Today, looking closer, I saw what I'd missed — a serious specialty bench hiding inside a vinyl-record listening bar. Walls of LPs, low amber light, coffee carried over in a glass carafe with a little ceramic cup. And in that cup, something I'd never archived: not Arabica, but Coffea liberica.

The roaster promised

Root beer · tropical fruit punch · raspberry candy · rambutan · longan · sarsi.

The cup delivered

Braced for wild funk — got the opposite. Clean and gently sweet, a soft longan-and-tropical-fruit thread running through it, with a quiet root-beer / sarsi edge sitting in the background. Properly different, in the best way.

I'm usually all about clean washed coffees, and figured I'd just tolerate this one as a curiosity.
Walked out a convert.
